title: code-review-pr-scratchpad-sofia-patel
content:
Quick scratchpad for PR review and follow-ups - PR #8421 (kv-cache batching refactor)

High-level summary (my reading)
- Purpose: decouple batching logic from KV cache hot-path and introduce a batching planner that aggregates requests across multiple model instances. Aim is to reduce per-token overhead for short sequences and improve GPU utilization for long-run workloads.
- Major changes: new BatchingPlanner class, KVCursor abstraction, change to cache key format (prefix + seq_id), added metrics around batch_size_distribution and planner_latency, removed a few internal synchronous flush points.
- Risk areas: cache invalidation semantics (prefix change), threading and locking around KVCursor, fallback behavior when planner cannot form batches, backwards compatibility for saved cache snapshots.

Quick checklist (things to verify before approving)
- [ ] Tests: unit + integration cover old + new cache key formats (test_kv_snapshot_compat)
- [ ] Benchmarks: confirm perf numbers on staging (throughput, p95 latency) with 1. short sequences (<=32 tokens) and 2. mixed seq lengths
- [ ] Metrics: batch_size_distribution, planner_latency, kv_hit_ratio present and wired to telemetry
- [ ] Migration plan: snapshot compatibility; do we need a migration job? If yes, add tickets and docs
- [ ] Docstrings + comments: BatchingPlanner public API explained (inputs/outputs/assumptions)
- [ ] Locking: ensure no double-lock where KVCursor and global cache lock could deadlock (look for lock ordering)
- [ ] Canary / rollout plan: small percentage traffic -> monitor planner_latency and error rates

Notes on specific files / lines (rough, will link to PR comments)
- runtime/kv/cache_manager.py: changed key format at line ~210. Need explicit compatibility test and an env flag to toggle new format (runtime flag: ENABLE_NEW_KV_KEY_FMT). Otherwise hotfix rollback will be hairy.
- runtime/kv/cursor.py: KVCursor#advance uses an internal thread-local state. Potential issue when requests are retried -> we may leak cursor entries. Add explicit cleanup in finally block.
- runtime/batching/planner.py: planner makes a best-effort to merge small requests; algorithm OK but complexity O(n^2) in worst-case. Add a note or limit on candidate window (max 64 candidates) to cap CPU. Also add micro-benchmark for worst-case input.
- runtime/telemetry/metrics.py: new metrics names look fine, but metric tags missing model and route dimensions (need model_id and route_id) -- otherwise we can't slice by model.

Refactor suggestions (future follow-up PRs)
- Extract the planner heuristics into a strategy interface so we can A/B different heuristics (greedy vs cost-based). Keep current one as DefaultPlanner.
- Introduce a lightweight in-memory sampler for batch formation when traffic is bursty, to avoid O(n^2) costs.
- Move cache snapshot serialization responsibilities out of CacheManager to a SnapshotStore abstraction (single responsibility).

Follow-ups / TODOs assigned
- [ ] Add compatibility test + env flag: owner = Sofia (me); small PR to add test and flag. Ticket: ENG-1342
- [ ] Add model_id + route_id tags to metrics: owner = Ethan (needs telemetry review)
- [ ] Add planner candidate-window cap & micro-bench: owner = Lena (bench infra)
- [ ] Draft migration notes for ops (how to handle old snapshots): owner = Sofia; link to Confluence doc

Open questions / discussion items
- Is there a reason we changed the cache key format to include prefix + seq_id vs the previous (prefix + request_id)? Was request_id insufficient? I think seq_id aligns with prefix caching but we must ensure uniqueness across retries.
- Rollback plan: if new planner regresses, can we toggle off via env flag? Need a graceful fallback to previous batcher implementation — where does that live now?
- Snapshot compatibility: if we keep old snapshots, can new code read them? If not, do we run a one-off migration? Ops cost estimate?

Local testing notes (what I ran)
- Unit: ran pytest runtime/kv tests, all passing locally except flaky test_kv_snapshot (flaky due to timing)
- Perf: ran microbench harness with 8 simulated clients, saw +12% throughput for short sequences, p95 latency improved by ~8ms. Need staging numbers at scale (k80 x8 not representative).
- Memory: observed a small increase (~3%) in peak mem due to candidate buffering — acceptable but should monitor

Suggested PR comments (short lines to paste)
- "Could we add an env flag (ENABLE_NEW_KV_KEY_FMT) and a migration test that asserts old snapshots are still loadable? This will make rollbacks safer."
- "Planner: consider adding candidate-window cap to avoid O(n^2) behavior on worst-case traffic patterns; micro-bench included would be great."
- "Telemetry: please add model_id & route_id tags to the new metrics so we can slice-by-model/route in Console."

Misc small nits
- Typo in runtime/batching/planner.py docstring: s/heurisitc/heuristic/
- Remove a TODO left in cache_manager: "TODO: remove sync flush" — confirm it's intended to be removed now that planner handles flushes.

Priority next steps before merge (minimum)
- Add env flag for key format OR ensure snapshot compatibility test in CI.
- Add model_id tags on metrics.
- Add candidate-window cap or at least a TODO + ticket to avoid pathological CPU usage.

If folks want, I can open the small follow-up PRs (tests + flags) once this lands, but prefer to keep them in-flight and merge main refactor only when CI has the compatibility test.

Slack threads / PR links for context:
- slack: #eng-runtime thread "kv-cache batching" (Dec 2025)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/8421
- Jira: ENG-1287 (design doc), ENG-1342 (compat test)

End of scratchpad. Will convert key points into PR comments and small follow-up PRs.
